cand.title: AI for Good Global Summit 2027
cand.organizationName: International Telecommunication Union with UN partners and Government of Switzerland
cand.excerpt: Published programme scale and airport-corridor venue are strong, but current access is constrained by Palexpo and unknown housing.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Verified organizer contacts, not verified hotel-contract buyers: Julien Smith, ITU Event logistics and virtual events manager, manages summit logistics and is the strongest operational routing contact; Frederic Werner, ITU Chief, Strategic Engagement Department & AI for Good / Chief of Strategy and Operations for AI for Good, is a strategic escalation contact. Jennifer Chalk, ITU Partnerships Manager, is an additional partnerships lead. No source establishes that any of these people controls hotel procurement or signs accommodation contracts.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced upcoming edition: 21–24 June 2027, Palexpo, Geneva, Switzerland, within the requested horizon. Actual activities begin with exhibitions, networking and curated activities on 21–22 June; the official opening is 23 June, followed by stage programming and workshops on 23–24 June. Do not reduce the activity dates to 23–24 June. The back-to-back Swiss Geneva AI Summit is a separate event, not an extension of these dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment/inference: selective airport-corridor lodging and small delegation/exhibitor/production-team meetings are plausible, but no such booking demand is confirmed. YOTEL is in Founex, Vaud, rather than at Palexpo or downtown Geneva. Its six meeting spaces, 23–352 sqm and up to 250 delegates, suit satellite briefings/training, not relocation of this large summit. Use the supplied 20–120-room commercial band only as a proposal boundary, not a published event requirement. The hotel advertises an airport shuttle morning/evening, no midday service and no pre-booking; this is not a contracted Palexpo shuttle. Any group proposal needs a separately costed, capacity-checked event transfer plan. This is a business-hotel opportunity, not evidence of a resort retreat requirement.
findings.venueCommitments: Published venue: Palexpo International Exhibition and Convention Center, Route François-Peyrot 30, 1218 Le Grand-Saconnex, canton of Geneva, Switzerland. Territory: Geneva Airport corridor, not Founex/Nyon/La Côte, not central Geneva, and not Lausanne. Palexpo is a convention/exhibition centre, not a competing hotel. The official venue announcement establishes the intended venue, not disclosure of the underlying signed contract.
findings.historicalRotation: The series has remained Geneva-based while changing venues: ITU headquarters in 2017–2018; CICG in 2019, 2023 and 2024; Palexpo in 2025–2026 and announced for 2027. This supports recurring Geneva relationship development, not an available rotating-destination host bid. Historical editions below separate past activity from the upcoming edition.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027 official FAQ: “We have secured exclusive preferential rates at selected hotels for AI for Good Global Summit attendees through our official accommodation partner.” It continues: “The link to book your accommodation will be provided soon.” The practical-information page marks accommodation “Coming soon.” Thus an official negotiated-rate channel already exists, but the 2027 partner identity, hotel names, allocation quantities and supplier-entry terms are undisclosed. Every 2027 hotel explicitly named in these official accommodation materials: none. This is not evidence of open sourcing or a guaranteed/committed room block. Historically, the 2026 official booking link points to Revolugo (wid=ai-for-good-2026); do not carry that partner appointment or inventory forward to 2027. The historical portal did not expose a readable hotel inventory; no complete historical hotel list or room-night total was verified.
findings.organizationStructure: ITU is the UN specialized agency organizing AI for Good, in partnership with over 50 UN partners and co-convened with the Government of Switzerland. This is an intergovernmental/UN-led event, not a trade association, corporate-owned conference, PCO or DMC. Palexpo is the venue, not the event owner. An official accommodation partner is acknowledged for 2027 but not named in the reviewed official materials; no independent PCO appointment was verified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: 2027 selected hotels already have negotiated attendee rates through an official channel, creating an incumbent-channel hurdle; hotel names and exclusivity are not disclosed. There is no verified evidence of sold-out hotels, unmet demand, overflow allocations or an open RFP. Palexpo is convenient to the airport and public transport, whereas Founex requires transfer planning. Published scale must not be converted into room demand: the historical 2026 total of over 12,000 participants from 177 countries covers AI for Good plus WSIS Forum/Geneva Digital Week, not summit-only attendance or overnight guests.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Use the official Engage contact route to request routing to Julien Smith and the 2027 accommodation lead; copy/escalate to Frederic Werner where appropriate. Ask who operates the 2027 hotel programme, whether additional properties can join, what room-allocation/commission/cancellation terms apply, whether separate delegation or exhibitor bookings are permitted, and when future supplier reviews occur. Only then offer a bounded 20–120-room proposal plus optional small meeting/F&B space and a separately costed Palexpo transfer plan. Do not hold the whole hotel, promise overflow, or approach Revolugo as the confirmed 2027 buyer.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the upcoming 2027 edition, the main summit venue is already announced and preferential hotel rates are already negotiated. Accessibility for YOTEL remains unconfirmed: neither inclusion in the official inventory nor an invitation to quote was found. Pursue a supplier-introduction conversation and separately arranged subgroups only after demand and channel rules are confirmed; do not label the event an open hotel tender.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated Geneva editions justify relationship-building for later accommodation allocations and small organizer/partner groups, not a forecast of automatic overflow or a host-venue displacement. No next-after-2027 exact edition dates/venue were verified; do not populate a 2028 opportunity with assumed June dates. Seek the supplier review timetable for subsequent editions once the 2027 partner and decision pathway are identified.
